instructions: Turn on the waffle iron to heat. If it has a temperature dial, set it to 400°F. Heat the oven to 200°F and set a wire rack on a baking sheet.
Melt the 1/3 cup butter in a small pan over low heat or in the microwave, then let it cool for a few minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk the 2 cups flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt.
Separate the 2 eggs, with the whites in a clean medium bowl and the yolks in another bowl.
Whisk the 1 2/3 cups milk, the melted butter and 1 tsp vanilla into the yolks.
Beat the whites with a hand mixer on medium high for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're thick and glossy and a peak stands straight up when you lift the beaters.
Pour the yolk mixture into the flour and stir with a spatula until there's no dry flour left. A few lumps are fine.
Add the whites and fold them in gently with the spatula. Stop as soon as the big streaks of white are gone, or the waffles come out flat.

Brush the hot iron with a little of the oil. Spoon in enough batter to cover most of the grid, close the lid and cook for 3 to 5 minutes. They're done when they're golden and the steam coming out the sides has almost stopped.
Move the waffle to the rack in the oven. Cook the rest of the batter the same way, brushing the iron with a little more oil when it starts to stick. You'll get about 6 waffles.

To freeze any extras, let them cool completely on the rack. Freeze them in a single layer on the baking sheet for 1 hour, then pack them into a freezer bag. Reheat them straight from frozen in the toaster for 2 to 3 minutes, until hot and crisp.
method_notes: Both mix the dry ingredients, whisk in milk, eggs, vanilla and melted butter and cook in a hot iron until golden, 3 to 6 minutes. Spend With Pennies separates the eggs and folds in whites beaten to stiff peaks for a lighter waffle, with 2 eggs and 1/3 cup butter to 2 cups flour. RecipeTin Eats uses 4 whole eggs and much more butter and suggests resting the batter in the fridge for 2 hours or overnight. This follows Spend With Pennies, whose batch makes about 6 waffles, and adds freezing and toaster reheating for school mornings. Double every amount for a freezer batch.
